decisions.question: Q1 resolve-in-place: does each row show the exact CLI command (or a POST write route), or only what a human needs to brief their agent?

options.text: show the exact CLI command per row

viewer read-only, no CLI command text; rows carry id, plain-English ask or finding, chain location, link to full context and what resolved looks like; a one-line copy handle (id plus ask) is a design candidate shown in the wireframe

decisions.answer: b. Product owner ruling 2026-10-07: the viewer stays read-only and shows no CLI commands. Quote: I meant provide the info they need to resolve with their agent. Keep the commands out of the view. The user operates their agent which uses these commands; showing them here is little value. Rows carry id, ask or finding, chain location, link, resolved state; the copy handle is a candidate ruled on the render.

decisions.question: Q2 delta on an unfrozen tree: render every document row on first paint, or counts only with on-demand expand?

options.text: every document row on first paint
counts only with on-demand expand

decisions.answer: b. Ruling 2026-10-07: counts only, on-demand expand.

decisions.question: Q3 thin requirements table: which flavours feed it?

options.text: the three product-owner checks only (as today)
all three flavours: zero criteria, unresolved tests, D4 floor failures (plus no story and no plain description)

decisions.answer: b. Ruling 2026-10-07: all three flavours, zero criteria, unresolved tests, D4 floor failures.

decisions.question: Q4 freeze-now: keep a button, show only the command text, or show the state and what resolves it with no button and no command text?

options.text: keep the button
command text only
no freeze button, no command text; show the state and what resolves it

decisions.answer: c. Ruling 2026-10-07: no freeze button, no command text; show the state and what resolves it.

decisions.question: Q5 Readiness layout: sub-tabs (Overview, Questions, Blocking, Coverage, Trace) or one long page with anchor navigation?

options.text: sub-tabs
one long page

decisions.answer: a. Product owner render ruling 2026-10-07: sub-tabs (Overview, Questions, Blocking, Coverage, Trace); the one long page alternative is retired.

decisions.question: Q1 schema home: does the journey record stay rcf-lite-local like the ledgers, with only the FBS journeyStepIds field going to rcf-schemas 0.7, or is the declaration mirrored onto manifest.intakeClassification from day one?

options.text: rcf-lite-local record under rcf/discovery/; only journeyStepIds to schemas 0.7; no manifest mirror
mirror the declaration onto the manifest in a second schemas change

decisions.answer: a. DISCOVERY verdict 2026-10-09 (engineering): journey.json rcf-lite-local like the ledgers (ADR-4121); only FBS journeyStepIds goes to rcf-schemas 0.7; no manifest mirror. ADR-4142.

decisions.question: Q2 legacy rollout: warn for one release then bite, bite immediately where inference says UI, or grandfather existing trees with no rollout mechanism?

options.text: warn for one release, then fail on an absent declaration
bite immediately on every tree the fallback inference calls UI
grandfather existing trees by absence of the record; no warn window, no retirement; doctor advises only

decisions.answer: c. Product owner ruling 2026-10-09: old projects land safely as they already exist; no warn-then-bite release train and no cliff; the gate applies to intake after the release and to any tree that re-runs intake. ADR-4145.

decisions.question: Q3 interruption catalogue v1 membership and the shape of the check: the four from the incident, or the six from the ux-designer role; drawn, or answered?

options.text: four entries from the incident (lostEmail, abandonedMidway, expiredLink, wrongDevice)
six entries from the ux-designer role (lostEmail, closedTab, deadBattery, expiredLink, switchedDevice, lostSignal), each answered by a step or notApplicable with a reason of 20 or more characters

decisions.answer: b. Product owner ruling 2026-10-09: the six from the ux-designer role, answered-or-notApplicable with a reason; the check is answered, not drawn. ADR-4143.

decisions.question: Q4 wireframe file types and the gate shape: markdown only with a heading-structure check, or markdown default plus self-contained HTML plus PNG for migration, hashed as bytes with no heading check; and is the declaration boolean or three-valued?

options.text: markdown only; Shape, States and Behaviour headings checked; boolean uiBearing
markdown default, self-contained HTML, PNG for as-built migration; bytes hashed, headings never inspected; three-valued none, light, central with wireframes required for central only

decisions.answer: b. Product owner ruling 2026-10-09: the gate is not tight; three values; wireframe richness is better input, never mandated; only central refuses for a missing wireframe. Engineering: markdown, self-contained HTML, PNG migration only; hash bytes never headings. ADR-4143, ADR-4144.

decisions.question: Q5 reviewer: single reviewer in v1, or a second-reader flag on journey review from the start?

options.text: single reviewer; a second reader only after the first missed dead end
a --litmus n second reader from the start

decisions.answer: a. DISCOVERY verdict 2026-10-09 (engineering): single reviewer in v1; a second reader only after the first missed dead end. ADR-4146.

decisions.question: Q6 build binding posture: is a UI-bearing build spec with no journeyStepIds refused at mark complete, or reported as a build review finding with no new hard gate at BUILD?

options.text: refuse at rcf build mark complete in the same block as the design gate
report as a build review finding (journeyStub) and show the state in the queue; the only hard gate is the DEFINE door

decisions.answer: b. DEFINE 2026-10-09: the accepted proposal states no new hard gate at BUILD and the product owner posture is not tight; the binding is visibility (queue, show, bundle, review finding), the DEFINE door is the only refusal. Deviation from the proposal's mark-complete line, flagged for the reviewer.

decisions.question: Q7 drawing requirements from journey steps: does this release carry the brief-statement source span journey:<stepId> and a D1 check brief:journeySteps (every step of a light or central product has at least one brief statement sourced to it), or does it carry only the record, the gate and the FBS binding, with the D1 check in the next DEFINE?

options.text: this release: journey:<stepId> source spans and the brief:journeySteps D1 check under REQ-189

next DEFINE: this release ships the record, the D0 gate and the FBS binding; the D1 check gets its own requirement once a tree has drawn requirements from a journey and the shape of a step-sourced statement is known

decisions.answer: b. DEFINE FINALISE 2026-10-09: this release ships the record, the D0 gate and the FBS binding (REQ-189). Drawing requirements from steps (journey:<stepId> source spans, a brief:journeySteps D1 check) is carried to the next DEFINE as its own requirement; the verdict is silent on it and the shape of a step-sourced statement is best set once a tree has drawn requirements from a real journey. Named as a carried item in the PR body.

decisions.question: (a) Finalise preconditions and exit codes: which preconditions refuse and with which codes?

options.text: FBS complete (4), HEAD on the default branch (4), --ci-run <ref> given and recorded (4 when absent; the CI status itself is not fetched in v1), every bound AC with a Code Node (3, matching mark complete), a Test-stage report present (4) and valid (3); provenance failures (4); retired --mode/--url (2)
same set, but Finalise queries the CI provider for the merge commit status (needs network and a token)
drop the CI precondition; branch protection already requires green CI before merge

decisions.answer: a. Exit 4 for every refusal of state or evidence, 3 for validation and missing Code Nodes (the mark-complete precedent), 2 for usage. CI is recorded by reference, not fetched: Finalise stays network-free and worker-runnable. Fetching CI status is a named later option.

decisions.question: (b) The verify report: where it lives, its schema, whether the verifier commits it, and whether committing it counts as editing.

options.text: in tree at rcf/verify-reports/<fbs-id>/<headSha12>.json, VerifyReport v1 (reportVersion, fbsId, headSha, target {kind url|package, url, packageRef}, mode, hand, verifierId, startedAt, finishedAt, rcfLiteVersion, verdict, verdictAuthority, runStats.counts, perAc[]), rcf-lite-local, committed by the verifier on the PR branch under Hand: verifier; a report file is evidence and does not count as editing production code, tests or criteria
out of tree (artefact store) referenced by hash on the FBS (needs an rcf-schemas FBS field)
in tree but committed by the stage-keeper after merge

decisions.answer: a. Reviewable in the PR, no schema change, walker-invisible like rcf/discovery/. The verifier still edits no production code, test or criterion; the separation check classes rcf/verify-reports/ as verifier evidence (ADR-4149).

decisions.question: (c) Provenance checks before Finalise writes verified.

options.text: report headSha is an ancestor of HEAD, or its tree equals the tree of a commit HEAD contains (squash merges); target is not loopback (localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1, 0.0.0.0); report hand is verifier and its verifierId matches no Hand-Id trailer on a Hand: builder commit in the merged range; finishedAt within --max-report-age, default 7 days
ancestry only (forbid squash merges on RCF build PRs)
a, plus Finalise re-probes the deployed URL

decisions.answer: a. 24 of the last 30 merged PRs here were squashed, so ancestry alone would refuse most merges; tree equality covers the squash case and forces a re-verify only when main moved under the PR. The hand check is as strong as the trailers (self-declared), which the scoped Review gate backstops.

decisions.question: (d) What happens to agentScreenshotCritique?

options.text: becomes an rcf verify run mode the verifier may use at Test for subjective visual criteria; leaves Finalise; URL-verifiable criteria resolve through the probe catalog; subjective criteria stay critique-only
retired entirely; subjective criteria are verified by a person

decisions.answer: a. Recommended. Consequence named: a spec with subjective criteria needs a Test-stage session allowed to run the critique mode; it no longer blocks Finalise itself.

decisions.question: (e) The backstop in rcf build bundle --next: refusal, override and adoption.

options.text: refuse exit 4 while any FBS at or above the adopted fromBuildOrder is complete and not verified; --allow-unverified "<reason>" proceeds and appends { reason, by, at, unverifiedFbsIds } to rcf/define/backstop.json; a tree without backstop.json is grandfathered; rcf build backstop adopt --from <fbs-id> writes the window
refuse on every complete unverified FBS in the tree, no window (would block this repository at once: none of its 107 FBS is verified)
reuse --override and freeze.override

decisions.answer: a. A separate flag keeps freeze overrides and verification overrides apart in the record. Whether the window holds is decision pending the operator (see the backstop decision below).

decisions.question: (f1) Separation: how a commit declares its hand.

options.text: Hand: trailer plus path inference; a declared hand must agree with its paths; an undeclared single-class commit passes
trailer required on every commit

decisions.answer: a. DISCOVERY PR 365 recommendation 1; --require-hand gives b per repository when wanted.

decisions.question: (f2) Separation: commits that touch both test and production classes.

options.text: fail, with one escape: Hand: mixed plus a non-empty Separation-Reason:, counted on the report line
always fail

decisions.answer: a. DISCOVERY recommendation 2 (the ADR-4131 posture: the gate bites, the acknowledgement is recorded).

decisions.question: (f3) Separation: where it runs.

options.text: rcf audit separation in CI on pull_request with fetch-depth 0, no hook in v1
also a pre-push hook installed by rcf init

decisions.answer: a. DISCOVERY recommendation 3.

decisions.question: (f4) Separation: path classes.

options.text: defaults matching at any depth, optional override rcf/separation.json (inside rcf/, so test-author territory); rcf/code-nodes/ builder, rcf/verify-reports/ verifier, rcf/fbs/ and rcf/manifest.json neutral
a required per-repo config

decisions.answer: a. DISCOVERY recommendation 4, extended with the verifier evidence class (ADR-4149). Named gap: rcf/fbs/ is neutral, so a builder could edit an FBS acIds unseen.

decisions.question: (f5) Separation: posture.

options.text: opt-in per repository; rcf-lite adopts from this DEFINE forward with no retroactive audit
separation as the default build cycle in the same release

decisions.answer: a. DISCOVERY recommendation 5. This DEFINE train already carries Hand: test-author on every commit.

decisions.question: (f6) Separation: trailer vocabulary.

options.text: the five estate hand names (test-author, builder, reviewer, verifier, stage-keeper) plus mixed
the DISCOVERY values test and build plus mixed

decisions.answer: a. The verifier report commit and the stage-keeper commits would otherwise be undeclared or mixed; one vocabulary across briefs, trailers and reports (ADR-4149). test and build are not accepted as aliases.

decisions.question: (g) Issue 349 scope and its schema dependency.

options.text: optional probe object on the acceptanceCriterion subschema (an @stravica-ai/rcf-schemas minor) plus rcf/verify-catalog.json keyed by acId, AC-level probe wins; the deterministic engine resolves pass, fail or skipped per AC with evidence; --parity-env honoured
catalog file only, no schema change
schema fields only, no catalog

decisions.answer: a. Build-ordering constraint: the rcf-schemas minor must publish and be pinned before FBS-218 merges ($defs/acceptanceCriterion is additionalProperties false today). The catalog alone would work without it, so b is the fallback if the schema minor slips.

decisions.question: (h) Guidance, managed block and attest-to-audit changes the Build hand makes.

options.text: FBS-224 rewrites guidance/build-cycle.md stages 1, 4 and 5 and the playbook to the five hands and the Test-stage report, updates the bundle closing runbook, regenerates the managed agent-instructions block with a non-null minAgentAction, and fixes README.md line 49 (define, build, verify, release, audit)
guidance changes ride with each behavioural FBS

decisions.answer: a. One guidance train after the behaviour exists, so the text never describes a verb that has not shipped. The attest grep found one fifth-verb hit (README.md:49); the other attest hits are the AC attestation field family and --litmus-attested, which are unrelated and stay.

decisions.question: (i) Sizing and build order.

options.text: seven FBS: FBS-218 probes (schema first), FBS-219 report, FBS-220 Finalise, FBS-221 backstop, FBS-222 separation verb, FBS-223 separation wiring, FBS-224 guidance
three FBS (verify and Finalise, separation, guidance)

decisions.answer: a. Each FBS fits one test-author, builder and verifier round; FBS-220 is the largest and the first candidate to split (ingest versus provenance) if its Define round shows more than eight tests.

decisions.question: PENDING OPERATOR: may the builder hand create Code Nodes through rcf define create cn?

options.text: yes, Code Nodes are the one chain write a builder makes (rcf/code-nodes/ is builder class in the separation check)
no, the test-author writes Code Nodes too

decisions.answer: a. Operator ruling 2026-10-16 12:45Z: yes, the builder creates Code Nodes through rcf define create cn; it is the one chain write a builder makes.

decisions.question: PENDING OPERATOR: are test-suite and test-case records written at Define by the test-author hand?

options.text: yes, at each FBS's own Define stage, with the tests; this chain-level DEFINE writes none
written by the verifier at Test

decisions.answer: a. Operator ruling 2026-10-16 12:45Z: yes, test-suite and test-case records are written at each FBS's own Define stage by the test-author hand, with the tests.

decisions.question: PENDING OPERATOR: does the backstop block on every merged unverified spec?

options.text: yes within the adopted window: rcf-lite adopts with rcf build backstop adopt --from FBS-218, and its 107 earlier specs (none verified) stay grandfathered
yes on every merged unverified spec in the tree, with no window (blocks this repository until the backlog is verified or overridden)

decisions.answer: Operator ruling 2026-10-16 12:45Z: yes, the backstop blocks on every merged unverified spec. Scope rule from this DEFINE: within the repo's adopted window, so a repo adopting mid-life names its first adopted FBS and older specs are grandfathered; a product that adopted from its first spec blocks on all of them.

decisions.question: PENDING OPERATOR: how does the Test-stage verifier obtain prerequisites (service sandboxes, auth accounts, an Access service token) when it runs rcf verify run against the preview or version host? Evidence 2026-10-16: 16 of 18 complete specs on a GBP 249 product refused with BLOCKED-PROVISIONING because the lane host holds no credentials and the operator surface sits behind Cloudflare Access.

options.text: the repo declares a provisioning profile (prerequisite kinds and credential references, never values); the stage-keeper's environment supplies the references at Test; verify run records which were supplied and marks the rest BLOCKED-PROVISIONING with the kind
criteria that need provisioning are verified by CI-profile tests with a declared parity claim; the deployed run covers only unauthenticated routes
no provisioning in the Test stage; the operator verifies provisioned criteria by hand

decisions.answer: Operator ruling 2026-10-16 15:5xZ: the orchestrator supplies the prerequisites at Test time (Dave as stage-keeper, or a human RCF operator), from per-repo operational notes kept outside the repo and outside the chain (library docs). The chain keeps only its existing service declarations (what is needed), never where or how. Supply is confirmed with the operator as a preflight once the DEFINE passes readiness. rcf verify run accepts the supplied prerequisites as environment or arguments and records which were supplied.

decisions.question: PENDING OPERATOR: criteria that are repository or CI properties (a workflow exists, a lint runs, a secret is never printed) have no live route on a deployed host. Evidence 2026-10-16: whole specs (CI workflows, deploy pipeline, operations register) came back DEGRADED with every criterion not exercised. How are they verified in the Test stage?

options.text: the probe catalog gains a ci probe kind; such criteria resolve from the CI run the verifier names (--ci-run), and the deployed-URL run skips them with reason ci-property
they are excluded from verify run and counted verified by the Review gate alone

decisions.answer: Operator ruling 2026-10-16: these criteria are obviously testable, not against a runtime, and the chain already distinguishes this through the runtime-profile vocabulary (deployed, ci, local-dev) on test cases. No new classification. verify run exercises only criteria whose test cases carry the deployed profile against the URL; ci-profile criteria are proven by the CI run the stage-keeper names (--ci-run) and are skipped on the URL run with reason ci-profile; readiness requires every criterion to have a test case with a declared profile.

decisions.question: Test-stage action policy for verify run. Operator ruling 2026-10-16 15:0xZ: a sandbox exists to be used; the up-front decision per integration is either provide the sandbox or test double and let the verifier use it, or mark that route not auto-verifiable. The 2026-10-12 rule covers real money only.

options.text: purchases, card entry and webhook posting are allowed when the target declares a sandbox for that integration (declared in the provisioning profile) and are recorded on the report; denied and resolved BLOCKED-BY-POLICY where no sandbox is declared; never against a live billing mode
default deny everywhere with a per-run opt-in flag

decisions.answer: a. Operator ruling 2026-10-16: yes, a declared sandbox is for the verifier to use; not much of a sandbox test otherwise. Purchases, card entry and webhook posting allowed where the integration declares a sandbox (supplied by the orchestrator per decision 30) and recorded on the report; blocked by policy where none is declared; never against live billing.

decisions.question: Operator ruling 2026-10-16: how did criteria with no live route (CI workflows, deploy pipeline) reach Build, and why was host capability not checked before the Finalise run? Both are DEFINE and stage-keeper defects, not tool defects. What does the chain require so this family of issue (verification route never decided up front; same family as the 2026-07 persona findings) stops recurring?

options.text: every acceptance criterion declares at DEFINE a verification route (deployedUrl | ciRun | manual | notAutoTestable) and runtime profile, plus the prerequisites it needs (service, sandbox or test double, account); define readiness refuses a tree with any criterion silent on route; rcf build bundle --next emits the per-spec prerequisite list; a stage-keeper preflight verb compares that list with the host before any Test or Finalise dispatch and refuses to launch what the host cannot meet
keep classification at Test time (verifier marks not exercised) and rely on briefs

decisions.answer: a. Operator ruling 2026-10-16: not testable criteria are obvious at DEFINE and at readiness; host capability is checked before dispatch; sandbox or test-double integrations are decided up front per integration. Decided, not pending.

decisions.question: (a) Suite-as-probe: kind or mode. A suite probe kind per criterion, or a package target mode that resolves every in-scope criterion through its TS/TC bindings? And what happens to a criterion that carries an HTTP probe under a package target?

options.text: package target mode: with --artefact or --package <dir> and no --url, every in-scope AC resolves through its existing TS/TC bindings, no per-AC probe authored, no acProbe change; HTTP probes stay for URL targets; an AC carrying an HTTP probe under package target mode resolves through its bound tests and records probeNotRun "package target has no served URL"
a suite probe kind on the AC or in rcf/verify-catalog.json naming a TS, TC or test file (needs an rcf-schemas acProbe change and per-AC authoring)

decisions.answer: a. Recommended option taken by the DEFINE hand (brief 2026-10-19): every criterion is already bound at its own Define stage (ledger 28), so the mode needs no per-AC authoring and no schema change. Recorded in ADR-4150, TAC-4151 and AC-19301-5.

decisions.question: (b) How do the bound tests reach the packed artefact?

options.text: copy method: copy the installed package into the scratch project and the bound test files' top-level directory beside it, so the tests' relative bin/rcf.js and the #core imports map resolve to the artefact; no test edits
an environment override for the binary path (every suite edited to read it)
redirected module resolution (a loader) in the clone

decisions.answer: a. Recommended option taken by the DEFINE hand: the method the three verifier rounds of 2026-10-17 proved, with no test edits. Recorded in ADR-4150 and TAC-4151.

decisions.question: (c) Install network and store policy for the packed artefact.

options.text: npm install --no-audit --no-fund <tgz> in a scratch project under os.tmpdir(), registry as the host configures it by default; --offline installs from the local npm cache only; the install command, exit code, registry (default | offline) and a log path are evidence on the report; an install failure exits 1 with the log path and writes no report JSON; Finalise stays network-free either way
offline by default, registry only on an explicit --online
a vendored local store under the repository

decisions.question: (d) Result mapping from per-test results to per-AC verdicts, and the exit codes.

options.text: an AC passes only when every test bound to it ran and passed (at least one); a bound test that is todo or skip makes the AC skipped; a bound title absent from the run makes it fail (notRun); no bound TC makes it critiqueOnly; verdict PASS when all passed, FAIL when any failed, BLOCKED otherwise; any non-pass means authority correctness; ship only when every in-scope AC passed; exit 0 written and PASS, 4 written and not PASS, 2 usage, 1 IO
an AC passes when any bound test passes

decisions.answer: a. Recommended option taken by the DEFINE hand, with one addition the chain forces: a bound test whose title does not appear in the run fails the AC as notRun, so a rename without its testPointer cannot pass silently (AC-19301-4). Exit codes as TAC-4148 states for rcf verify run.

decisions.question: (e) Report fields for a tool-written package-target report, and where raw evidence lives.

options.text: additive VerifyReport v1 fields: method suiteAsProbe; profile packagedArtefact; target { kind package, packageRef, name, version, sha256, servedSha (HEAD when packed, null for a given --artefact) }; pack and install records; suites[] per-suite counts; runStats.counts.critiqueOnly; perAc evidence with TC ids, test titles and reporter test numbers; raw reporter output and install log in a sibling directory rcf/verify-reports/<fbs-id>/<headSha12>/, walker-invisible, verifier evidence, ignored by Finalise's *.json lookup
raw output embedded inside the report JSON

decisions.answer: a. Recommended option taken by the DEFINE hand: the report stays small and readable in the PR, the raw output is reviewable beside it. servedSha is null for a given --artefact because a tarball names no head; FBS-226 records HEAD when it packs. Profile value named packagedArtefact, the name the rcf-schemas 0.9.0 brief proposed.

decisions.question: (f) Finalise and the interim ruling: does rcf build finalise --ci-run ingest the tool-written report unchanged, and should it refuse a hand-composed report once suite-as-probe ships?

options.text: Finalise ingests it unchanged (every field is additive; target.kind package with packageRef and perAc results already pass verifyReportFault), proven end to end by AC-19301-9; no refusal of hand-composed reports in this spec; the interim ruling of 2026-10-17 is superseded once FBS-225 ships (ADR-4150): the stage-keeper accepts only a tool-written report for a new CLI-product Test stage; the guidance text naming the hand-composed route (the Test-stage paragraph of the five-stage contract that FBS-224 writes, and the verifier role's Test-stage method outside this repo) changes with the build
Finalise refuses a report without method suiteAsProbe for package targets

decisions.answer: a. Recommended option taken by the DEFINE hand. The three hand-composed reports on main (FBS-218, FBS-219, FBS-220) stay valid history. FBS-225's own Test stage runs under the interim ruling, since the tool cannot verify itself before it exists; FBS-226 is the first Test stage the tool runs.

decisions.question: (g) Kept behaviour from FBS-219 under package target mode.

options.text: kept: exactly one --fbs, a dirty tree outside rcf/verify-reports/ refuses exit 4, an existing report for the same head refuses exit 4 unless --replace "<reason>", writes only under rcf/verify-reports/<fbs-id>/; and --package <name@version> or a tarball name that is not a directory keeps the FBS-219 record-only behaviour (AC-19001-4), so no verified criterion is superseded

decisions.answer: a. Recommended option taken by the DEFINE hand (AC-19301-7, AC-19301-8, AC-19302-5).

decisions.question: (h) Position in the train: where do FBS-225 and FBS-226 sit against FBS-221 to 224? rcf define create fbs refuses a buildOrder equal to an existing one ("--build-order 221 collides with FBS-221 (existing buildOrder=221) under BS-001") and no free integer lies between 221 and 222, so both were created at the default buildOrders 225 and 226 and the queue lists them after FBS-224.

options.text: the operator approves renumbering through the CLI: rcf define update FBS-222, FBS-223, FBS-224 --set buildOrder to 227, 228, 229, then FBS-225 and FBS-226 to 222 and 223 (edits FBS-222 to 224's buildOrder only; goldens and count pins move)
the operator approves rcf define update FBS-225 --set buildOrder=221 and FBS-226 likewise, relying on the queue's fbsId tie-break; this bypasses the create verb's collision guard
leave 225 and 226 after FBS-224; FBS-222 to 224's Test stages then run under the interim hand-composed method, and FBS-224's guidance cannot name the tool yet

decisions.question: (i) Sizing: one FBS or two?

options.text: two in order: FBS-225 (install, copy, run, mapping, report, end-to-end Finalise; 9 ACs) then FBS-226 (pack from HEAD, install policy; 5 ACs), each one test-author, builder and verifier round under 40 minutes
one FBS with all 14 ACs

decisions.question: (j) Where do VerifyReport v1 and the profile enum live, and does this spec need the in-flight rcf-schemas 0.9.0 release?

options.text: VerifyReport v1 is rcf-lite-local (src/verify/report/index.js writes it, src/finalise/ingest.js validates it; the rcf-schemas 0.9.0 round, PR 24 decision 4, left the packed-artefact fields to this DEFINE), so packagedArtefact and the artefact identity are rcf-lite-local; the deployed | ci | local-dev enum lives in rcf-schemas manifest.schema.json browserVerify.runtimeProfile (test-suite runtimeProvenance.profile is a different enum: mock | stub | fixture | live | mixed) and is not written by this path; no rcf-schemas field is needed; if the 0.9.0 pin bump rides FBS-225's build, 0.9.0 must be published and pinned before FBS-225 merges (build-ordering constraint)

decisions.answer: a. Checked by the DEFINE hand against the rcf-schemas 0.8.0 package pinned in this repo and the 0.9.0 round's record; recorded in TAC-4151 internalStructure and the FBS-225 notes.
